Lichen planus is a skin disorder generally con- trolled with corticosteroids (see p.1580), although ciclosporin has also been used. Ciclosporin has been given successfully in relatively low doses (3 to 5 mg/kg by mouth) to produce remis- sion of severe lichen planus,1 but such therapy may be associated with the development of hypertension and impairment of renal function. Use of topical ciclosporin for oral lichen planus has been tried, but results have been variable.2-8 One such study failed to note any benefit long-term from either ciclosporin mouthwash or corticosteroid oral paste.7 1.
